trust_decision.summary: Whether an element is kept or discarded is decided by animatesUrlAttribute() inside sanitizeHtml's onopentag, on the element's attributeName TARGET (href in any namespace prefix, or any entry of options.allowedSchemesAppliedToAttributes) rather than on the animation's own values/from/to/by, so an `<animate attributeName="href">` is dropped before any of its URL-bearing value attributes are inspected.

landing_point.why: The summary says "URI-list scheme-policy bypass", and this is the only place in the package where the URL scheme policy is applied to attribute values (gated by options.allowedSchemesAppliedToAttributes), so a reader who has only the summary expects the fix to extend this check to list entries.

fix_sites.entry_point: sanitizeHtml(html, options) module export (index.js:64) — condition gains `|| animatesUrlAttribute(name, attribs)` so a rejected animation is skipped like a disallowed tag
fix_sites.module_kind: published library (npm package `sanitize-html`, single default export)

fix_sites.entry_point: same export — module-level constants svgAnimationTags and alwaysUrlAttributes added after vulnerableTags
same export — internal helper animatesUrlAttribute() inserted in the sanitizeHtml closure between naughtyHref and parseUrl

O3_reason_to_dismiss: naughtyHref is a generic shared string helper in a different package used for every URL field (launder.url, link fields), so a solver can argue the vulnerable component is the SVG animation element handling in sanitize-html, not the primitive — and hardening the primitive by rejecting any value containing ';' would reject legitimate URLs.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Animations of presentation attributes that are not URL sinks (fill, opacity) and non-animation elements that merely carry an attributeName attribute must keep their tags/attributes; and legitimate URLs containing ';' must keep passing naughtyHref. A fix that rejects any element carrying attributeName, or that rejects any value containing ';', breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: semicolon-separated `values` list with a safe first entry (`#safe;javascript:...`) versus a single value
the alternative value attributes `from`, `to` and `by` in place of `values`
namespaced target `xlink:href` versus bare `href` (local name taken after the last ':')
mixed case and surrounding whitespace in `attributeName` (`" HREF "`)
targets other than links that the scheme policy covers (e.g. `src`), i.e. any entry of allowedSchemesAppliedToAttributes
each of the five animation element names (animate, animateColor, animateMotion, animateTransform, set), matched case-insensitively
an animation whose value attributes are not in allowedAttributes at all (rejected on the target alone)
allowedTags: false / disallowedTagsMode escape and recursiveEscape (rejected element escapes as inert text)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SMIL animation targeting a URL list attribute the sanitizer scheme-checks but that is not in allowedSchemesAppliedToAttributes: `<animate attributeName="srcset" values="javascript:alert(1)">` survives, although the static `srcset`/`imagesrcset` attribute is scheme-checked entry by entry (index.js:443-468) and the option list at index.js:990-997 omits both names; the fix builds its target set only from that option list plus `href`.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: srcset is absent from allowedSchemesAppliedToAttributes and SMIL cannot retarget an HTML-only attribute on an SVG element, so the animation is inert in a browser.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~170 lines from the landing point (index.js:443 versus index.js:374); no package hop

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Plain space-separated URL-list attributes that ARE in the default scheme-checked list — `ping` and `archive`: the entire value is handed to naughtyHref as one URL, whose cleanHref strips whitespace (launder/index.js:11) and whose matcher reads only the leading scheme (launder/index.js:49), so `ping="https://ok.example javascript:alert(1)"` keeps the disallowed entry, unchanged by the fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: `ping` is a fire-and-forget beacon list and `archive` a legacy object hint, neither a script or navigation sink, so the surviving entry cannot execute — the same "list validated as one URL" mechanism, but with no XSS sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, plus the shared primitive one package away in packages/launder

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A general per-entry scheme check for any attribute that holds several URLs (space-separated `ping`/`archive`, or SMIL `values`), reusing the parseSrcset/naughtyHref-per-entry loop.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The maintainer already wrote exactly this per-entry loop for srcset and imagesrcset in the same function, so extending it to other list-valued attributes is the natural next refactor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A rich-text/area configuration (an `svg` or `animate` toolbar item) whose toolbarToAllowedTags/toolbarToAllowedAttributes actually enable the precondition mentioned in the advisory.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: optionsToSanitizeHtml is purely data-driven off the editor toolbar, and SVG icons/animation are a plausible rich-text feature for an Apostrophe site, so a maintainer could add that allowlist entry.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another small first-party package that widens the rich text widget's allowedTags/allowedAttributes (as this one does for `span`/`style`).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This module already ships extendMethods that push tags and attributes into the sanitize-html options, so a second one that widens tag sets is a copy-paste-away change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A list-aware sibling helper (naughtyHrefs(list, separator)) next to naughtyHref, exported statically like naughtyHref at index.js:538.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: launder is already the shared home of the scheme primitive that sanitize-html imports, so a list variant belongs there and wiring it in is one line.

O9_family: Cross-site scripting (CWE-79): HTML-sanitizer URL scheme policy bypass via a post-sanitization attribute write

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm 10.18 workspace (root package.json:33); package needs Node >= 22.12.0 (packages/sanitize-html/package.json:28-30); mocha 11 for tests and eslint 9 for lint (packages/sanitize-html/package.json:10-13); no compile step
O10_build.project_tests: packages/sanitize-html/test/test.js (mocha; `npm test` also runs eslint), no database required (`apostropheTestConfig.requiresMongo: false`, packages/sanitize-html/package.json:46-48); existing scheme-policy coverage for URL lists at test/test.js:960-999 (srcset) and test/test.js:1074-1091 (imagesrcset)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Split the `values` attribute on ';' and scheme-check each entry (or make naughtyHref reject any value that contains a second scheme), which still leaves `from`/`to`/`by`, namespace-prefixed targets and the srcset-style target set open.

out_of_scope_notes: The second listed fix commit 38ff1106c8 is a "Stable reconciliation q2 m3 2026" merge that bundles fixes for OTHER advisories and unrelated bugs (server-side prototype pollution GHSA-vmg4-6gfg-83qx in packages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/util/index.js, the patchWidgetIfSuitable shortcut in page/piece-type/schema, position-based schema field _ids, email field laundering, session regeneration on password change, a Sass BOM fix, an Astro proxy redirect-header fix, a sharp bump); none of it belongs to GHSA-g8qq-57p8-ggw5 and I did not pursue it.

The candidate metadata (c_fix_sites 30, c_site_files 16, c_same_check_name patchWidgetIfSuitable) is derived from that reconciliation merge, not from this advisory; advisory-scoped source changes are one file, packages/sanitize-html/index.js.

The changeset for this advisory states the default configuration and `apostrophecms` itself were not affected because the SVG animation elements are not in the default allowedTags, so the real deployment surface is an application that adds them (fix.diff:15).

Browser-side exploitability of an `<animate attributeName="srcset">` (whether any engine honours such a target) was reasoned from the specification's attribute types, not tested; it is listed as a code-consistency uncovered route, not a proven live bypass.
